title: Japan's Paternity Leave Rate Topped 50% in 2025
paragraphs: In Japan, more fathers are taking time off work to take care of their babies. For the first time, more than half of new fathers took childcare leave.

According to Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, 50.9% of men took childcare leave in the 2025 fiscal year. This is 10.4 percentage points higher than the year before. The number has gone up for 13 years in a row.
The ministry surveyed about 6,300 workplaces. It looked at people whose children were born between October 2023 and September 2024.

The biggest change was at small companies. At workplaces with 5 to 29 workers, 42.9% of men took leave. A year earlier, the number was only 25.1%. At large companies with 500 or more workers, the number was 60.7%.

However, there is still a big difference between men and women. About 88.3% of women took childcare leave. Women also took much longer leave. The most common length for women was 12 to 18 months. For men, it was one to three months.

The Japanese government wants more fathers to take leave. Its goal was 50% by 2025, and now its new goal is 85% by 2030. Companies must now tell workers about childcare leave when they say they are having a baby.
Japan is trying to help families because its birth rate is very low. The number of Japanese citizens recently fell below 120 million for the first time in more than 40 years.
